Ford Bronco Dahaidao Edition Debuts in China, So This Is What We're Missing
7 photos
Photo: Ford
Ford unveiled the all-new Bronco Dahaidao Edition in China, and it looks like it could fit right in in the United States. The new off-road-focused variant is scheduled to make public debut at the Guangzhou Auto Show later this week with Bronco Heritage Edition-like looks and 35-inch off-road tires.
The all-new Ford Bronco Dahiadao Edition is inspired by the Bronco' s racing heritage at the Baja 1000 and named after China’s uninhabited Dahaidao Gobi desert crossing in Xinjiang. The model is finished in vibrant red and features a removable white hardtop, contrasting black wheel arches, and large white "BRONCO" decals so onlookers know what they're dealing with.
The off-roader rides on two-tone silver and black beadlock-capable wheels with all-terrain tires. It sports front and rear differentials, stands at 10.75 inches (273 millimeters) of ground clearance on FOX 2.5-inch shock absorbers, and has a wading depth of 33.4 inches (850 millimeters), backed by underbody steel skid plates and high-clearance fenders, all confirming its off-road abilities.
Built on a body-on-frame chassis and sitting on the Ford T6 platform, just like its American sibling, the special edition is offered exclusively as a four-door. Those doors open to a cabin that is different from what we all know from the U.S.-spec Bronco .
Photo: Ford China Unlike the model selling in America, the Chinese Broncos run an upgraded system powered by a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8155 chip on a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster and a 12-inch central touchscreen.
The Chinese Bronco retains physical rubberized buttons and toggle switches on the center console for the locking diffs and 4WD modes, plus the overhead auxiliary switches pre-wired for aftermarket lights or winches. Rugged, easy-to-clean upholstery, a Bang & Olufsen sound system, and PVC washout flooring with drain plugs are also on the menu in typical off-road fashion.
Under the hood of the Dahaidao Edition sits the 2.3-liter EcoBoost turbocharged inline-four, the only option available in China. The inline-four produces 271 horsepower (275 metric horsepower) and 316 pound-feet (429 Newton meters) of torque. A ten-speed automatic transmission puts the power down through all four corners.
The all-new Bronco Dahaidao Edition will roll off the production line of the Jiangling-Ford joint venture starting this winter. Ford has no plans to bring it to North America, where the closest visual and mechanical equivalents are the Bronco Heritage Edition when it comes to the red-and-white retro appearance, and the Sasquatch Package, which also rides on 35-inch tires.
Photo: Ford China The automaker hasn’t disclosed pricing details yet, but it will probably do so during the Guangzhou Auto Show later this week. The all-new Ford Bronco Dahaidao Edition is expected to start at around 299,800 yuan, which translates to roughly $41,500. In the U.S., the similar Bronco Heritage Edition is a $52,620 deal.
